title: Wages Accounted for 30.8 Percent of Mexico’s GDP in the First Quarter
author: Alejandro Alegría
content:
_This article by Alejandro Alegría originally appeared in the[August 28, 2026
edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/08/28/economia/salarios-
representaron-el-308-por-ciento-del-pib-en-el-primer-trimestre-inegi),
Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. In the first quarter of 2026, **wages in the Mexican economy
represented 30.8 percent** , **an advance of 4.1 percentage points compared to
2018** , the National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI) reported
this Friday. According to the Quarterly Institutional Sector Accounts (CSIT),
in January–March of this year, employee compensation showed an advance of 1.7
percentage points compared to the same period of 2025, when wages represented
29.1 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

According to the information published by INEGI, over the last eight years a
positive trend has been observed in the share of compensation, which went from
representing 26.7 percent of GDP in the first quarter of 2018 to 30.8 percent
in the same period this year.

By contrast, **corporate profits in the country represented 39.4 percent** of
the Mexican economy in the reference period, a decrease of 1.7 percent
compared to January–March 2025. Nonetheless, compared to the first quarter of
2018, when it stood at 46.7, the **contraction is 7.3 percentage points**.

This shows that **the distribution of wealth in the country has changed
significantly over the last 8 years, benefiting the population that receives
compensation**.

In the first quarter of 2026, Mexico's GDP was 35.5 trillion pesos in current
terms. Of this amount, 10.9 trillion pesos correspond to employee compensation
and 14 trillion pesos to corporate profits.

Separately, according to INEGI, households generated 35.0 percent of the
Mexican economy in the first quarter of 2026, an advance of 0.6 percentage
points compared to the same period last year. Businesses in Mexican territory
contributed 43.5 percent of the country's GDP, a contraction of 1.5 percentage
points compared to January–March 2025.

Financial corporations represented 5.2 percent of the Mexican economy, a
slight increase of 0.1 percentage points compared to the first quarter of the
previous year. Meanwhile, the federal government contributed 8.2 percent of
GDP in January–March 2026, an increase of 0.6 percentage points compared to
the same period a year earlier. For their part, nonprofit institutions serving
households represented 0.8 percent of the Mexican economy in the reference
period, with no change compared to the first quarter of 2025.
